_layout: SINCE 2026-10-21 (r36) THE APPLY ORDER IS ONE FILE PER MIGRATION, in this directory:
Order = seq ascending (numeric), then file name. History is numbered 10, 20, ... so an
insertion fits between two neighbours (a fraction is fine). Two lanes that each add one
migration touch two different paths and merge with zero conflicts; a seq tie after such a
merge breaks by name. This _manifest.json holds everything that is not per-migration.
Place a new migration:   node tools/apply-order-split.mjs --add <file.sql> --note "STAGED, NOT APPLIED - ..."
Lane still on the old tests/schema-apply-order.json:   node tools/apply-order-split.mjs --migrate
Readers: tools/lib/apply-order.mjs loadApplyOrder() (the old single-object shape).
The _readme below is the history of the single file; "this file" there means this directory.
_readme: THE APPLY ORDER OF supabase/migrations/**. This is the single source of truth
for rebuilding the database from the repo, and it is verified on every push by
tests/schema-drift.mjs (via tests/schema-replay.mjs).
WHY THIS FILE HAS TO EXIST. Filename order does NOT replay. Measured
2026-08-14: applying supabase/schema.sql + every migration in filename order
gets 23 of 41 files in and fails the other 18. Two reasons, both structural:
1. '2026-08-08-clan-seat-2.sql' sorts BEFORE '2026-08-08-clan-seat.sql',
because '-' (0x2D) < '.' (0x2E). The -2 file's first act is to check that
clan_board exists and raise if it does not, so it fails first, every time.
2. Nine files are dated 2026-08-11 and alphabetical order puts 'accrual',
'accrue-gate', 'anon-execute-lockdown', 'apply-engine' and
'authenticated-surface-lockdown' all BEFORE 'player-state' â€” which is the
foundation every one of them depends on. There is no naming scheme that
rescues this after the fact.
Before this file, the working order existed only as a hand-maintained const
array inside tests/pglite-chain.mjs and another inside
tests/conservation-fuzz.mjs, each covering a DIFFERENT SUBSET of the
migrations, and neither one covering all of them. That means the order
required to rebuild the database was not written down anywhere.
RULES:
Â· Every .sql file in supabase/migrations/ must appear exactly once, across
'pre_schema', 'order' and 'excluded'. The guard FAILS on a file that is in
none of them â€” so a new migration cannot be silently left out of the
rebuild. The full apply sequence is: pre_schema, then supabase/schema.sql,
then order.
Â· A new migration goes where it actually has to run, not where its date
puts it.
Â· 'excluded' is a claim that a rebuilt database is CORRECT without the file.
Never add one to make the chain go green.

_why: GUCs production was actually applied with, not shortcuts.
it, and production was applied with it set on 2026-08-13 (that is what closed
A11). A rebuild that omitted it would leave beta_invites world-readable and
the file would tell you so, loudly.
market_wipe_ok: read by 2026-08-17-market-v2.sql, which is in 'order'
(staged; it supersedes and deletes the old 2026-08-11-market-v2.sql). The
GUC gates that file's DROP...CASCADE of the live market tables.

_pre_schema_why: supabase/schema.sql creates game_saves and game_events with `create table if
not exists` as a bootstrap fallback, and its own header says they are assumed
to already exist. Those fallback definitions do not match production: different
primary key on game_saves, different COLUMN NAMES on game_events (kind vs
event_type, created_at vs occurred_at). Running the true shapes first makes
schema.sql's fallback no-op on a rebuild exactly as it no-ops on production.
The alternative â€” ALTER + rename the columns afterwards â€” is a rename on the
table holding every player's save, which cannot be rolled forward past a
failure. Ordering is reversible; that is not.

excluded.2026-08-12-clan-members-rls-drop.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED, and it REFUSES to apply by design: its precondition needs a real clan_ledger row of kind='member', i.e. a player who joined through clan_join(). A fresh rebuild has no such row, so the file correctly raises. That refusal is the file working, not the chain failing.
excluded.2026-09-13-town-presence-off.sql: STAGED - KILL SWITCH, apply ONLY on incident, then re-measure restore-census. EXCLUDED from the replay chain deliberately, and the exclusion is the CLAIM this key is for: a rebuilt database must come back in the SHIPPING state - The Common ON, per 2026-09-13-town-presence-on.sql - and a chain that ran this file after it would rebuild the feature DARK while every record said it was live. One idempotent `update public.hr_flags set enabled = false, updated_at = now() where key = 'town_presence' and enabled is distinct from false`, plus a two-assertion gate: the row reads false, and hr_town_of() answers off:true read AS A SIGNED-IN CALLER (an unauthenticated read is refused and would satisfy a weaker assertion for the wrong reason). No function body, grant, policy, object or value touched. It does NOT stop hr_heartbeat - last_seen_at keeps being stamped, nothing reads it while the flag is down, and turning the flag back on repopulates the plaza on the next 25-second tick with no backfill - and it does NOT touch presence_quiet, so a player's opt-out survives the incident and the recovery. Security condition on b32a3f5a (GO-with-changes). Reversibility: re-apply 2026-09-13-town-presence-on.sql. AFTER APPLYING: move hr_flags.live_value to enabled=false in tests/restore-census.baseline.json, or the deployment record lies in the direction that costs a day of debugging.
